title: Service Mesh Zero-Trust Architecture with Istio, Envoy Sidecars, mTLS & SPIFFE Identity
problem: Microservice topologies operating on Kubernetes clusters leave east-west (service-to-service) network traffic unencrypted and unauthenticated by default. In the event of a single pod breach, lateral attacker movement across internal cluster networks is trivial due to cleartext HTTP communications, static IP trust assumptions, and absence of granular Layer 7 authorization policies. Furthermore, lack of unified traffic management makes progressive canary rollouts risky and creates blind spots in distributed service latency tracing. This project builds a production-grade zero-trust service mesh architecture on Kubernetes using Istio and Envoy. The platform enforces strict mutual TLS (mTLS) with cryptographically verified SPIFFE identities, implements fine-grained authorization policies and Layer 7 traffic routing (canary splits, circuit breaking), exports telemetry to Prometheus, and visualizes live dependency topologies via Kiali with under 3.5ms proxy latency overhead.

use_cases.title: FinTech Core Banking Microservice East-West Encryption
use_cases.first_sentence: Financial microservices transferring customer fund balances across internal payment and ledger services must comply with zero-trust regulatory mandates.
use_cases.second_sentence: Istio sidecars automatically enforce mutual TLS across all inter-service connections, ensuring encrypted data in transit with rotated X.509 certificates and SPIFFE IDs.

use_cases.title: Progressive Canary Traffic Shifting for High-Volume APIs
use_cases.first_sentence: Platform engineering teams releasing new versions of customer-facing recommendation services need automated canary deployments without traffic disruption.
use_cases.second_sentence: The service mesh splits production traffic dynamically (e.g. 90% v1, 10% v2) using Istio VirtualService weights, monitoring error rates before promoting releases.

use_cases.title: Resilient Microservice Cascading Failure Prevention
use_cases.first_sentence: E-commerce checkout pipelines relying on downstream inventory microservices risk cascading cluster failure during inventory database connection stalls.
use_cases.second_sentence: Envoy circuit breakers trip when consecutive 5xx errors exceed thresholds, failing fast with cached responses and isolating failing pods from healthy cluster tiers.

hard_parts: Configuring Istio mutual TLS (mTLS) in STRICT mode across multi-namespace Kubernetes clusters with automated SPIFFE certificate issuance and rotation
Writing fine-grained Istio AuthorizationPolicy resources restricting pod-to-pod RPC communication using authenticated SPIFFE identities and HTTP method rules
Implementing advanced traffic management with VirtualServices and DestinationRules governing canary percentage splits and outlier detection circuit breaking
Minimizing Envoy proxy latency overhead and CPU utilization under high-throughput microservice request volumes using optimized filter chains
screener_signals: Clean Kubernetes and Istio configuration repository cleanly separating namespace manifests, VirtualService routes, AuthorizationPolicies, and Prometheus dashboards
Security penetration benchmark report proving 100 of 100 unauthorized inter-service plaintext connection attempts are blocked by strict mTLS
Anti-fake verification script sending an unauthenticated HTTP request from a rogue curl pod to an internal payment service and asserting connection termination via SSL handshake failure

architecture.data_flow: A user request enters via the Istio Ingress Gateway; the gateway verifies TLS and routes to the frontend microservice; the frontend Envoy sidecar establishes an mTLS connection to the backend payment service Envoy sidecar; sidecars exchange and validate SPIFFE X.509 certificates issued by Istiod; the payment service's Istio AuthorizationPolicy evaluates the client SPIFFE ID; if authorized, the request forwards to the local application container over localhost; Envoy streams access metrics to Prometheus; Kiali queries Prometheus to render real-time service dependency graphs; when a canary deployment triggers, VirtualService routing splits 10% of traffic to the v2 payment pod.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Cryptographic TLS handshake verification rejecting non-SPIFFE certificates; Envoy L7 filter chain evaluating RBAC policies at kernel socket boundaries.

targets.method: Wall-clock round-trip latency added by Envoy sidecar proxy interception compared to direct pod-to-pod baseline under 1,000 RPS
targets.input: 10,000 requests issued through 3 microservice mesh hops at 1,000 requests per second
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Minikube / Kind local Kubernetes cluster with Istio 1.18+
targets.minimum_pass: p95 proxy latency overhead per hop is < 5.0 milliseconds
targets.target: p95 proxy latency overhead per hop is < 2.2 milliseconds
targets.report: Envoy proxy latency benchmark report and latency percentile table

targets.metric: STRICT mTLS Unauthorized Connection Block Rate
targets.method: Percentage of unauthorized plaintext or invalid-certificate connection attempts rejected by Envoy sidecars
targets.input: 50 connection attempts from non-mesh pods or pods with forged certificates targeting internal services
targets.environment: Local Kubernetes cluster with PeerAuthentication mode set to STRICT across all namespaces
targets.minimum_pass: 50 of 50 unauthorized connection attempts terminated with SSL handshake failure
targets.target: 50 of 50 unauthorized connection attempts terminated with SSL handshake failure
targets.report: mTLS security enforcement audit log and TLS handshake rejection trace

targets.method: Observed percentage of requests routed to canary v2 deployment compared to configured VirtualService weight (10%)
targets.input: 5,000 synthetic HTTP GET requests issued to canary-instrumented service endpoint
targets.environment: Istio VirtualService configured with 90% weight to v1 and 10% weight to v2
targets.minimum_pass: Observed canary traffic split is within 9.0% to 11.0% across 5,000 requests
targets.target: Observed canary traffic split is within 9.5% to 10.5% across 5,000 requests
targets.report: Canary traffic routing distribution log and Prometheus metrics export

environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source stack using local Minikube / Kind in Docker Desktop)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or managed cloud Kubernetes clusters required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Docker Desktop, Minikube / Kind (Kubernetes 1.26+), kubectl, and Istioctl installed

riskiest_component.name: Cluster-Wide Outages from Misconfigured STRICT mTLS Policies
riskiest_component.mitigation: Deploy mTLS initially in PERMISSIVE mode while verifying Prometheus mTLS telemetry, then transition to STRICT.
riskiest_component.fallback: Emergency Istio PeerAuthentication patch reverting namespace to PERMISSIVE mode.
